summary.headline: ABLBL Q4 FY26 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR 2,174 crores, with consolidated EBITDA up 14% to INR 375 crores and margin at 17.2%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered double-digit revenue growth of 12% YoY, led by Lifestyle Brands (+11%) and Emerging Businesses (+18%), with retail like-to-like at 6%. Consolidated EBITDA rose 14% to INR 375 crores and margin expanded about 20 bps to 17.2%, helped by a one-time PLI benefit of about INR 20 crores in the quarter. Reported PAT was INR 55 crores after a one-time labour code exceptional item; normalized PAT was INR 60 crores (+58%). Management flagged softer wedding demand and moderating sentiment late in the quarter from geopolitical uncertainty and volatility.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 38 crores YoY; includes one-time labour code exceptional item
vs INR 781 crores in March last year

financial_highlights.metric: Operating cash flow before capex and security deposit FY26

segments.name: Lifestyle Brands
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 1,829 crores, +11% YoY, EBITDA margin about 20%. FY26 revenue INR 7,154 crores with FY26 like-for-like growth of 8% and margin 19.6% (+20 bps). Management says all Lifestyle brands grew at similar rates.

segments.name: Emerging Business (Reebok, Van Heusen Innerwear, American Eagle)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue +18% YoY across 390+ stores; EBITDA margin up 420 bps YoY. Management puts FY26 Emerging Business EBITDA at about 4%, up from roughly breakeven last year.

segments.name: Reebok
segments.commentary: Q4 growth of 30%, with double-digit like-for-like for the year. Network is over 210 stores; full-year sales have more than doubled since acquisition three years ago.

segments.name: Van Heusen Innerwear
segments.commentary: Double-digit growth in Q4 and sharply lower full-year losses. Management targets at least one profitable quarter in FY27, with break-even previously guided for Q4 FY26.

segments.name: American Eagle
segments.commentary: Profitable, with double-digit like-for-like growth in the quarter.

segments.name: Contract manufacturing / Others channel
segments.commentary: Others channel rose sharply to roughly INR 120-130 crores from about INR 65-70 crores run rate, driven by contract manufacturing exports from a new Pulivendula factory plus institutional business.

guidance_outlook: Store additions of 300+ in FY26; footprint 3,348 stores, 4.9 million sq ft, nearly 800 cities and towns.
FY27 store closures expected at 3-5% of network; net expansion to be stronger than FY26 as closures fall.
FY27 expansion spend guided at INR 250-300 crores, of which about INR 200 crores is retail; capex about INR 300 crores.
Lifestyle like-for-like projected at about 7% over a steady-state period; Reebok to add 40-50 stores per year.
Dividend policy: 15-25% of net profit over time; net debt-free target of about three years, though not chased aggressively.
Van Heusen Innerwear: at least one profitable quarter in FY27, with Q3 FY27 a possible break-even quarter.
Working capital to be tightened in FY27, releasing cash from pre-produced inventory.
Lifestyle margins expected to see basis-point improvements, not dramatic expansion.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about INR 325 crores; FY27 capex guided at about INR 300 crores, with a slightly lower requirement than last year.
Capex split: routine capex INR 50-60 crores; expansion and renovations about INR 200 crores; balance on manufacturing and technology.
Company-operated stores are about 36-37% of the network, roughly 1,200-1,250 stores; franchise partners fund much of expansion.
New Pulivendula factory added capacity, supporting contract manufacturing growth; PLI benefit of about INR 20 crores booked in Q4 as a one-time item.
Project Stretch is enlarging existing stores; a typical store is refurbished once every five to six years.
demand_pricing: Wedding-led demand was uneven in Q4 due to a softer wedding calendar; consumer sentiment moderated late in the quarter on geopolitical uncertainty.
E-commerce and departmental stores each grew double digits in Q4; FY26 e-commerce was roughly flat after H1 rationalisation, with H2 growing strongly.
Management flagged crude-linked input cost pressure on polyester and bottom-wear. Autumn-winter buying is largely locked; impact is not yet quantified and may lag.
Management said margin pricing power was not discussed in quantified terms; ability to pass costs through depends on how inflation plays out.

qa_highlights.question: Cash flow: how will debt be repaid if working capital is high and capex stays at about INR 300 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital can be released this year from pre-produced inventory. Capex will be about INR 300 crores, with partner-led franchise expansion. Business will keep generating cash, stronger than this year.

qa_highlights.question: Others channel jump and PLI benefit: what drives it and how sustainable is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by contract manufacturing from the new Pulivendula factory plus institutional business. About INR 20 crores of PLI benefit landed in Q4 as a one-time item; management said Lifestyle margins expanded about 20 bps for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Store expansion: what is the FY27 pipeline and how many closures?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion targeted at INR 250-300 crores capex. Closures expected at 3-5% of the network, lower than FY26 (about 90 stores in a good year). Management said macro conditions will not materially affect store expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Van Heusen Innerwear: when does it turn profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: Targeting at least one profitable quarter in FY27, probably Q3. Revenue grew double digits, with focus on inventory and cost reduction. Steady-state profitability is about six quarters away.

qa_highlights.question: Emerging Business margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Emerging Business EBITDA margin moved from about breakeven last year to nearly 4% this year and should keep improving each quarter, led by Reebok scale and lower Van Heusen losses.

risks_watch: Q4 margin included a one-time PLI benefit of about INR 20 crores; underlying margin gain is smaller.
Crude-linked raw material inflation with a lag; FY27 margin impact not quantified.
Wedding calendar volatility and moderating sentiment; Lifestyle LTL guided to about 7% over a steady state.
Other expenses and gross margin trend in the consolidated P&L were questioned by analysts; management disputed the reading, and it was taken offline.
Van Heusen Innerwear profitability timing (at least one profitable quarter in FY27) and Reebok break-even ambition.
Standalone versus consolidated raw material cost difference was raised; management deferred to offline reconciliation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth momentum, Reebok and Emerging Business, but cautious on near-term demand and input costs, which management described as not yet visible in numbers. Management was evasive on margin headroom and on the consolidated other-expenses question, deferring several points offline.
key_quotes: Expansion momentum also remained robust, building further on the strong sales witnessed in last quarter, while emerging brands continued to see encouraging recovery and regained a sharp growth trajectory.
So, have we peaked out? No, not yet. But can you expect dramatic changes in margin profile? Not really.
Going ahead, there won't be a PLI scheme that you will get.

adds.what: Store additions: 300+ stores in FY26 (footprint 3,348 stores, 4.9 mn sq ft); FY27 net expansion stronger than FY26 with 3-5% closures
Reebok network adds 40-50 stores per year (network over 210 stores)
New Pulivendula factory (contract manufacturing) already added; capacity supports Others channel growth

growth.why: Management guided to ~7% steady-state Lifestyle like-for-like growth and FY27 store expansion spend of INR 250-300 crores (about INR 200 crores retail), with 40-50 Reebok stores a year, but gave no revenue growth number for FY27 and flagged softer wedding demand and input cost pressure.
